purpose: Exploit the sharp degree-four graph frontier by using a supplied Hamiltonian cycle as a global coordinate system. Encode every proper 3-colouring by one Boolean direction bit per Hamiltonian edge. All remaining graph edges become forbidden residues of interval sums over GF(3), yielding a linear-size exact Boolean interval-mod-3 avoidance carrier on a source class where 3-colourability is still NP-complete.

input.graph: A graph G with a specified Hamiltonian cycle H=(v_0,v_1,...,v_{n-1},v_0).
input.hard_source: In the degree-four source boundary every vertex has two H-edges and two complement edges, so E(G)\E(H) is a 2-factor, i.e. a disjoint union of cycles.

difference_encoding.fix_global_symmetry: Set c_0=0 in GF(3); every other 3-colouring is equivalent under a global colour shift to exactly one such colouring.
difference_encoding.hamiltonian_edge: Proper colouring requires c_{i+1}-c_i in {1,2}. Introduce b_i in {0,1} by c_{i+1}-c_i = 1+b_i mod 3.
difference_encoding.prefix_reconstruction: For j=1,...,n-1, c_j = j + sum_{k=0}^{j-1} b_k mod 3.
difference_encoding.cycle_closure: The final Hamiltonian edge v_{n-1}v_0 is proper together with closure c_n=c_0 exactly when n+sum_{k=0}^{n-1} b_k = 0 mod 3. Equivalently the oriented differences around H sum to zero.

complement_edge_constraints.orientation: For a non-H edge {v_i,v_j} choose 0<=i<j<=n-1 and the forward H interval I=[i,j).
complement_edge_constraints.properness: The edge is properly coloured iff sum_{k=i}^{j-1} b_k != -(j-i) mod 3.
complement_edge_constraints.carrier: Thus every complement edge forbids exactly one GF(3) residue of one consecutive-ones linear form in Boolean variables.

main_theorem.name: HAMILTONIAN_3COLOR_IFF_BOOLEAN_INTERVAL_F3_AVOIDANCE
main_theorem.statement: G is 3-colourable iff there exists b in {0,1}^n satisfying one global mod-3 cycle-closure equality and every complement-edge interval disequality above.
proof: Forward: from a proper colouring with c_0=0, each Hamiltonian difference is 1 or 2 and uniquely defines b_i. Telescoping around H gives the global closure equation, and every complement edge gives its interval disequality.

Backward: from b, define colours by the prefix formula. Every Hamiltonian edge has nonzero difference 1+b_i, global closure identifies c_n with c_0, and every complement interval disequality makes its endpoint colours distinct. Hence all graph edges are properly coloured.
The maps are linear-time and mutually reconstructing up to the fixed global colour shift.

prefix_gain_graph_view.prefix_bits: Let q_i=sum_{k=0}^{i-1} b_k mod3. Then b_i in {0,1} is the binary transition constraint q_{i+1}-q_i in {0,1}.
prefix_gain_graph_view.chord: Every complement edge becomes q_j-q_i != -(j-i) mod3.
prefix_gain_graph_view.interpretation: This is a 3-state gain-graph binary CSP in which each edge forbids exactly one difference in GF(3). The interval presentation and the gain-graph presentation are polynomially equivalent.

source_hardness_firewall.fact: 3-colourability remains NP-complete for 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs. Published restrictions keep a given Hamiltonian cycle and impose strong structure on the complementary 2-factor.
source_hardness_firewall.meaning: Consecutive-ones interval normals, one global GF(3) equation, Boolean coefficients and a complement 2-factor do not by themselves license a polynomial algorithm. A polynomial exact solver for this carrier would constitute genuine progress on P versus NP.

positive: A linear-size exact hard-source carrier with only Boolean variables and GF(3) interval linear forms.
Global colour symmetry is removed explicitly; witness reconstruction is a single prefix scan.
The carrier connects the graph-critical v5.0 frontier back to the AF3/hyperplane-avoidance algebraic language, but with the extra consecutive-ones structure absent from generic AF3.
anti_loop: Do not expand all 2^n Boolean direction strings.
Do not treat interval matrices being totally unimodular over the integers as a SAT algorithm: the constraints are modular disequalities on Boolean points, and the source class is NP-hard.
Do not drop the global cycle-closure equation.

next_target.name: E8_BOOLEAN_INTERVAL_F3_AVOIDANCE_CONTRACTION_V5_2
next_target.directive: Attack the exact interval carrier directly. Seek a polynomial zero/nonzero or minimax invariant exploiting consecutive-ones normals and complement-2-factor structure without enumerating Boolean strings, residues on O(n) boundaries, or generic high-degree monomials. Mandatory controls are K5 with a Hamiltonian cycle, 3-colourable 4-regular controls, and the NP-hard 4-regular Hamiltonian source class.

sources: Herbert Fleischner and Gert Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2), 2003.
Classical Brooks theorem and maximum-degree-four 3-colourability hardness sources from v5.0.
